pass_a_gloss: And according to some deeper accounts Isaiah declares: I gave Egypt and Ethiopia and Syene as a trade of you, on your behalf, from which time you became held in honour before me. The precise account about this and the remaining things, if loving learning in Christ and wishing already at some time to step over the learning by a glass and in an enigma you hurry toward the one who called, almost at once facing one another you will know, as friends of the father and instructor who is in the heavens. For the friends learn in form and not through enigmas, or by a wisdom naked of voices and wordings and tokens and patterns, striking upon the nature of the things known by the mind and the loveliness of truth. If indeed you trust that Paul was snatched to a third heaven and snatched into the garden and heard sayings not to be uttered, which it is not allowed for a human to talk of, consequently you will know that than the sayings not to be uttered then uncovered to Paul, after which he has gone down from the third heaven, more and greater things you will straightway know, not going to go down after the knowledge, if lifting the cross you follow behind Jesus, whom we have as great chief priest having gone through the heavens. And yourselves, not standing off from the place behind him, will go through the heavens, stepping over not only earth and the secret rites about earth but also heavens and the matters about them. For there are in God things laid by as treasure, spectacles much greater than these, which no nature among those in a body, if not first released from every body, is able to hold. For I am persuaded that than what sun and moon and the dance of stars beheld, and also than those of holy angels, whom God made wind and blaze of fire, much greater things God stores up and guards beside himself, so that he may make them manifest when all the made world is freed from the bondage of the enemy into the liberty of the glory of the offspring of God.
pass_b_english: And by certain deeper meanings Isaiah says: “I gave Egypt and Ethiopia and Syene as an exchange for you, since you became precious in my sight” (Isaiah 43:3-4). The exact account of this and of the rest you will know, and very soon, “face to face” (1 Corinthians 13:12), as friends of the Father and Teacher in heaven, if, as lovers of learning in Christ who want at last to pass beyond learning “through a mirror” and “in a riddle”, you hasten to the one who called you. For friends learn by plain sight and not through riddles, or by a wisdom stripped bare of sounds and words and symbols and types, as they come into touch with the nature of intelligible realities and the beauty of the truth.

If indeed you believe that Paul was caught up “to the third heaven” and “caught up into paradise and heard unspeakable words, which a human being is not permitted to speak” (2 Corinthians 12:2, 4), it follows that you will know this: you will at once come to know more and greater things than the unspeakable words then revealed to Paul, after which he came down from the third heaven; and after that knowledge you will not come down, if you take up the cross and follow behind Jesus, whom we have as “a great high priest who has passed through the heavens” (Hebrews 4:14). And you yourselves, not leaving your place behind him, will pass through the heavens, rising above not only the earth and the mysteries of the earth but also the heavens and the things that concern them.

For there are stored up in God sights far greater than these, which no nature of those in a body can take in unless it has first been set free from every body. For I am persuaded that God keeps in store and guards with himself things far greater than those the sun and the moon and the choir of the stars have seen, and greater even than those the holy angels have seen, whom God made “spirit” and “a flame of fire” (Psalm 104:4), so that he may reveal them when the whole “creation” is set free “from slavery to the enemy into the freedom of the glory of the children of God” (Romans 8:21).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 13); the old English was a digest. This chapter's text sat under old section 12, where ὅσον οὐδέπω ('very soon') became 'not yet' face to face and the closing clause on creation set free was cut off; old section 13 held a two-line digest of chapter 14.
Read ὅσον οὐδέπω, 'very soon' (all but now); the old English made it 'not yet'. M has οὐδέποτε.
Koetschau prints τοῦ ἐχθροῦ (M), 'slavery to the enemy'; P and Delarue have τῆς φθορᾶς, 'of corruption'. English follows Koetschau.
Rendered 'not leaving your place behind him', taking τῶν ὀπίσω as the place behind Jesus (the following of the cross just named).
Taken in parallel with ὧν εἶδεν: greater than what the holy angels have seen.
